{{Quote|Battle droid sentry 8557, investigate Turbine Control malfunction and report in.|A battle droid to 8557|<ref name="Star Wars: Obi-Wan">[[Star Wars: Obi-Wan (video game)|''Star Wars: Obi-Wan'']]</ref>}}
'''8557''' was a [[Gender/Legends|masculine-programmed]] [[B1-series battle droid/Legends|B1-series battle droid]] sentry assigned to a [[Trade Federation/Legends|Trade Federation]] [[Unidentified C-9979 landing craft|C-9979]] [[C-9979 landing craft/Legends|landing craft]]. 8557, like all B1 battle droids, had [[Color/Legends|black]] sensors. 8557 carried a [[E-5 blaster rifle/Legends|E-5 blaster rifle]]. In [[32 BBY/Legends|32 BBY]], the [[Jedi/Legends|Jedi]] [[Padawan/Legends|Padawan]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]] sneaked aboard 8557's landing craft and sabotaged the [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmospheric]] turbine [[Engine/Legends|engines]] to force the ship to land on [[Naboo/Legends|Naboo]]. Another [[Battle droid/Legends|battle droid]] ordered 8557 to investigate the malfunction in the Turbine Control room.

{{GameMechanics|legends=1|Star Wars: Obi-Wan (video game)}}
8557 encountered Kenobi, who cut down the [[Droid/Legends|droid]] sentry using his [[Obi-Wan Kenobi's first lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] before proceeding further into the ship.
{{Endgame}}

==Behind the scenes==
8557 appears in the ''Stowaway'' mission in the [[2001]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] [[Star Wars: Obi-Wan (video game)|''Star Wars: Obi-Wan'']] after the player, in the guise of Kenobi, disables the engines. It is not necessary to destroy 8557, but this article assumes the player cuts down every battle droid. Instead of using the lightsaber, players may use a [[Telekinesis/Legends|Force push]] to dispatch 8557. The droid was mentioned in the [[Star Wars: Obi-Wan: Prima's Official Strategy Guide|strategy guide]], which tells players to go through the door 8557 opened.
